runtime.execution: Compiled Lisp in a long-lived OS process; OS threads and child processes are explicit.
runtime.service_boundary: A runtime used by an application, not an agent or shared-computation governor.

summary: Live compilation and global-state core images are powerful primitives, with explicit thread, stream and runtime compatibility limits.

inspection.scope: Read save/deinit, source/FASL load, compile-file interface, process execution/control, thread interruption and save rejection tests.
inspection.limits: No complete compiler/runtime audit or execution of SBCL; no agent protocol or harness rebuild coordinator supplied.

actions.name: LOAD / COMPILE-FILE
actions.output: Loaded globals or FASL path, diagnostics and errors
actions.lifecycle: Live process; definitions may change future calls.

actions.name: SB-EXT:RUN-PROGRAM
actions.input: Executable, literal argv, directory, environment, PTY and IO options
actions.lifecycle: Wait by default; :wait nil gives ongoing process.

actions.name: SB-THREAD:INTERRUPT-THREAD
actions.lifecycle: FIFO interrupts; critical sections defer delivery.

actions.name: SB-EXT:SAVE-LISP-AND-DIE
actions.input: Core path, toplevel, executable flag and hooks
actions.output: Core or combined executable; current process exits
actions.lifecycle: Quiescent image snapshot; later startup at toplevel.
actions.authority: Application owns image and thread cleanup

evidence.claim: Images preserve global state, unwind stacks, change streams and require single-thread quiescence; even separately built runtimes are incompatible.
Save hooks precede checked live/starting/joinable-thread rejection and foreign teardown.
LOAD evaluates source or loads FASL into the current Lisp environment.
COMPILE-FILE returns FASL; block compilation may resolve function references at compilation time.
RUN-PROGRAM accepts literal argv, optional PTY/streams, wait flag, status hook and preserved descriptors.
Thread interrupts are asynchronous and FIFO but nonlocal transfer during cleanup may skip cleanup.
Startup real-time and process CPU time are separate interfaces.

tests.focus: Attempt to image-save while another thread is waiting.
tests.oracle: assert-error expects save-with-multiple-threads-error; second case checks finalizer remains a thread after rejected save.

strengths: Live native compilation and interactive redefinition without a JS host.
The image contract explicitly distinguishes globals from stacks, threads and OS streams.
limits: An image is tied to the exact runtime build; rebuilding the native runtime needs a separate data handoff.
Interrupts can disrupt cleanup; a disciplined quiescence protocol remains application work.
arconaut_questions: Can a data handoff preserve agent identity and context while leaving compiler/runtime images disposable?
Which mutable definitions are indirectly dispatched so activation can occur after turn/workflow conclusion?
